operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case table names (AwardsMisc, HOF, Teams, Coaches, Master, abbrev) and mixed-case columns (Type, Code, Fullname, Min, PostGP, SepW, JanW...); must double-quote identifiers.
Quoted identifiers with special chars: "R/P" (CombinedShutouts), "+/-" and "Post+/-" (Scoring), "T/OL" (Goalies).
Composite PKs everywhere: Teams(year,tmID), Coaches(coachID,year,tmID,stint), Goalies(playerID,year,stint), TeamVsTeam(year,tmID,oppID), TeamsHalf(year,tmID,half), abbrev(Type,Code).

Composite FKs: Coaches(year,tmID)->Teams(year,tmID); Goalies/GoaliesSC/GoaliesShootout/Scoring/ScoringSC/ScoringShootout/SeriesPost/TeamSplits/TeamVsTeam/TeamsHalf/TeamsPost/TeamsSC all reference Teams(year,tmID) or Teams(tmID,year) (reversed column order in TeamVsTeam.oppID and TeamsHalf.tmID).

FK to non-unique parent: Master.coachID -> Coaches(coachID) where coachID is only PK-part (composite PK), so parent column is NOT unique; same for AwardsCoaches.coachID, AwardsPlayers.playerID -> Master(playerID) (Master.playerID is not PK, not unique, 3.1% NULL).
Master has NO primary key (pk=[]); playerID is nullable and non-unique (7520 distinct of 7761).

Self-ish / multi-FK to same parent: CombinedShutouts has two FKs (IDgoalie1, IDgoalie2) both -> Master(playerID); SeriesPost has two FKs to Teams (tmIDWinner, tmIDLoser) plus year twice; TeamVsTeam has oppID,year and year,tmID both -> Teams.

Storage class contradicts declared type: many TEXT columns hold integer-looking strings (Teams.PIM/PPG/PPC/SHA/PKG/PKC/SHF/OTL/SoW/SoL, Goalies.GP/Min/W/L/GA/SA, Master.height/weight/birthYear/birthMon/birthDay/firstNHL/lastNHL, Scoring.PPG/PPA/SHG/SHA/GWG/GTG/SOG, TeamSplits month columns).
INTEGER columns that are really small enums: Teams.rank (10 distinct), Coaches.stint (3), TeamsHalf.half (2), CombinedShutouts.month (8)/date (27), ScoringShootout.stint (3).

Near-constant / single-value columns: AwardsMisc.award (1 distinct 'Patrick'), AwardsMisc.lgID (1 'NHL'), HOF.category (3), abbrev.Type (4), Teams.lgID (5), Coaches.lgID (5); many all-NULL columns (AwardsCoaches.note 100% NULL, TeamSplits.SepT 100% NULL, SepW/SepL/SepOL 99.9% NULL).
Large tables: Scoring 45967 rows, TeamVsTeam 25602, Master 7761, Goalies 4278 — under 300k cap but Scoring is the dominant read; read once per worker.
No views/triggers in DDL; only CREATE TABLE statements; FK actions ON UPDATE/DELETE CASCADE (irrelevant since fk pragma OFF at write).
operator_ts_expectations: All declared types are TEXT or INTEGER; no DATE/TIMESTAMP/BOOL/BIT/YEAR/CHAR(n) types, so TS dispatches every column to String or Number fuzzer only — no Date/Time/Bool fuzzers exercised on this DB.

String fuzzer on TEXT columns: random strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() of length 0..20, plus 5 sampled original values, plus literal-pool values; contaminate 50% (suffix/prefix/around/drop-char). Names like 'Sid Abel', 'Toronto', 'NHL' become random gibberish -> implausible values drive FN on equality/join predicates.

Number fuzzer on INTEGER columns: range [-10^4,10^4] (scale=4 default for bare INTEGER? actually int family scale from args, none -> scale default), perturbed +-1/+-2; year columns (1909..2011) get values like 5000, -3000 -> implausible years, FN on year filters.

Integer-looking TEXT columns (PIM, GP, W, PPG, birthYear, height, weight) get String fuzzer -> random letters, not numbers; queries comparing them numerically or to numeric literals will miss (FN) and joins on them break.

FK columns filled from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement: Teams(year,tmID) composite FK means Coaches.year and Coaches.tmID are drawn independently from Teams.year and Teams.tmID lists -> pairs (year,tmID) that never co-occur in Teams -> dangling composite FKs; same for Goalies, Scoring, TeamVsTeam, SeriesPost, TeamSplits, TeamsHalf, TeamsPost, TeamsSC, GoaliesSC, GoaliesShootout, ScoringSC, ScoringShootout.
Master.playerID is non-unique and nullable; AwardsPlayers.playerID, Goalies.playerID, Scoring.playerID draw from it with replacement -> duplicate playerIDs across child rows, and NULLs propagate.

PK dedup (sample_fresh_primary_keys) drops duplicate composite PK rows; unique-column dedup (drop_unique_duplicates) drops rows repeating a single unique column — but Master has no PK and no unique columns, so no dedup there; Teams/Coaches/Goalies/TeamVsTeam/TeamsHalf/abbrev get PK dedup.

NOT NULL not enforced in Python: rows violating notnull (e.g. Teams.year, Coaches.coachID/year/tmID/stint, Goalies.playerID/year/stint, AwardsPlayers.playerID/award/year, abbrev.Type/Code, Master.lastName) fail at insert and are skipped -> smaller-than-requested tables, possible empty tables.

Single-value columns (AwardsMisc.award='Patrick', lgID='NHL') get String fuzzer with 1 element -> mostly that element plus random strings; queries filtering award='Patrick' may still match but random strings add noise.

All-NULL columns (AwardsCoaches.note, TeamSplits.SepT) have empty original_values and empty literal pool -> String fuzzer with no elements -> p=1, always fresh random strings; queries IS NULL will miss (FN).

Literal pool from train SQL: values like 'NHL','WHA','First Team All-Star','Hart','C','D','G','L','R','Rookie','tie' seeded into String samplers; numeric literals (years 1909..2011, ranks) seeded into Number samplers via FK-root ancestor mapping — but ancestor mapping across Teams(year,tmID) composite may misroute values.

Known TS misses: FN from implausible random strings/numbers (year=5000, name='xQ3()'), FN from all-NULL columns never matching IS NULL, FP from missing ties/duplicates (PK dedup removes duplicate rows that real data has, e.g. Master.playerID duplicates), FP from composite-FK pairs that never co-occur.
